data.title: As Europe's balance of power shifts eastward, France & Spain seek to 'reinforce their own positions'
data.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Carlos Mascarell Vilar, political scientist based in Spain. From his own perspective, Emmanuel Macron's visit to Spain needs to be understood by European power, political legacy, and geoeconomics. France and Spain are seeking to reinforce their bilateral relationship at a moment when the balance of power within Europe is changing rapidly, particularly with the growing importance of countries in the east such as Poland. For Macron, strengthening the Madrid-Paris axis is also part of a broader effort to advance European defence and strategic sovereignty.

data.title: Migration deal: 'Really a scheme around political diplomacy between UK & France in post-Brexit era'
data.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Parvati Nair, Professor of Hispanic, Cultural and Migration Studies at Queen Mary University of London. She sees the UK-France migration agreement as a small but revealing element of a much wider post-Brexit relationship, in which questions of migration are intertwined with diplomacy, security, intelligence and surveillance. She warns that the scheme risks trivialising a complex human plight it into deterrence and a numbers game. She argues humans have always moved, and migration can profoundly enrich societies. The challenge is to build systems that recognise both national sovereignty and human dignity.

data.title: AI deepfake of BBC report falsely links Indians to FlyDubai hijacking attempt
data.description: False videos are circulating after the attempted hijacking of a FlyDubai flight between Dubai and Tel Aviv. One fake "BBC" report falsely claims an Indian passenger was behind the incident and links him to the stabbed pilot, Smit Machchhar. The video though, is an AI-generated deepfake: the BBC never broadcast it, and its footage and audio were doctored. A second clip was also misrepresented and filmed in Dubai, not over where the incident occurred. Vedika Bahl fact-checks in Truth or Fake.

data.title: It's true: this is my final column. You have exactly 24 hours to complain before my inbox self-destructs | Marina Hyde
data.description: Yes, after 25 years I’m signing off, and I’ve cherished every moment – especially storming the French embassy with a (toy) AK-47 Journalism 101 – a course I have yet to complete – dictates that if you have something salient to say you should get there fast. So right now, I should mention that this is my last ever column for the Guardian. I’ll level with you: I spent a long time wondering how to write it. At first, I thought it should be about all the things I’ve learned, purely because that would be a hell of a lot shorter than a column about all the things I keep failing to learn, no matter how many times I make the mistakes. For example: if you’ve got a good joke, you’d best put it in the intro. (Why is there literally no joke in this intro?) Or: remember that people love the piss-taking until it strays into the arena of something they like, when it suddenly becomes wholly unacceptable. Take the time I wrote: “Arguing on the internet is like playing real tennis: even if you win, you’re still a twat ”. This prompted an immediate missive from a member of the Cambridge University real tennis club, which appeared on the letters page under the headline “ Real tennis has been served badly by this unfair slur ” and began: “Like many Guardian readers, I have thoroughly enjoyed and always look forward to reading Marina Hyde’s witty and caustic commentaries on the world about us. However …” Incidentally, I told this story at one book tour event, and then at the signing afterwards, a lovely young lady came up to get a book dedicated to her father, Jeremy. And of course, she said: “I should probably mention, he’s the guy who wrote in from the Cambridge University real tennis club.” Truly, the circle of life. To Jeremy, and the many other Jeremies who have written in over the years, let me just say: we all know the real twats are rackets players. Marina Hyde is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: After rape allegations at Cornell University, why are women again being urged to talk to their sons? Why not men? | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: Boys learn by watching how the men they respect treat their partners, female colleagues, women on the street. Now is the time for those men to step up There were seven men in all, and it lasted almost seven hours. What followed, according to the woman at the heart of the Cornell University case that has gripped student campuses around the world, was less a sexual encounter than a grim pack-bonding exercise fuelled by booze and ketamine, in which she was passed around like a blow-up doll. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist In the UK, the Rape Crisis national freephone helpline is on 0808 802 9999 (12-2.30pm and 7-9.30pm every day of the year). Rape Crisis also operate a live chat helpline , open Monday: 2pm-4.30pm, 6pm-9pm; Tuesday: 2-4.30pm, 6pm-9pm; Wednesday: 12pm-2.30pm, 6pm-9pm; Thursday: 12pm-2.30pm, 6pm-9pm; Friday: 9am-11.30am, 2pm-4.30pm. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on 116 123 and also by email in Ireland jo@samaritans.ie . You can contact the mental health charity Mind by calling 0300 123 3393 or visiting mind.org.uk . The 24-hour freephone National Domestic Abuse Helpline, run by Refuge , is on 0808 2000 247. In the US, Rainn offers support on 800-656-4673 . In Australia, support is available at 1800Respect (1800 737 732). Other international helplines can be found at ibiblio.org/rcip/internl.html Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: ‘It’s a deep soul connection’: Erasure on how 40 years of friendship got them through grief – and why Vince Clarke has quit touring
data.description: Returning for a 20th album of sumptuous synthpop, Andy Bell and Clarke open up about difficult recent years, being happily uncool and battling resurgent homophobia Andy Bell is rabbiting away on multiple topics. There’s his farm in Mallorca, where he and his husband Stephen Moss have had a fine year harvesting pomegranates, kiwis and lemons. Then there’s the Erasure frontman’s fascination with clowns (“Would the makeup help you avoid facial recognition technology?”), memories of 90s nightclubbing (“You could do anything and get away with it!”) and a worry that he’s turning into “a fussy old grandpa”. Suddenly, he catches himself: “But what about you , Vince? You’re being very quiet!” Bell’s bandmate, whose only contribution since joining the video chat from his San Diego home has been to say hello, smiles. “No, no, I just love listening to you, man. I’m really enjoying this.” Continue reading...

data.title: May heatwaves, deaths, ruined harvests: study of Europe’s summer paints grim picture for the future
data.description: EU Copernicus report shows surface air temperatures from June to August were 2.5C above decadal average The scorching heat that persistently baked western Europe this summer was the worst on record, a report has found, with more than half the continent seared by “very strong” heat stress that felt hotter than 38C. Surface air temperatures in western Europe from June to August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average, according to an update from the EU’s Copernicus climate monitoring service on Friday, while milder but still deadly heat across the rest of the continent made the summer Europe’s third hottest on record. My instinct was to put my hands under hot water, but that made it worse. For a while, that’s all I experienced. I thought it was weird but not dangerous. data.title: Calls grow for US death penalty halt after ‘torturous’ botched execution of Christa Pike
data.description: Pike alive but in critical condition as experts call ordeal that unfolded in Tennessee Wednesday ‘unimaginably barbaric’ Top lawyers, doctors and members of the faith community are calling for a moratorium on the US death penalty after Tennessee’s failed attempt to execute Christa Pike left the prisoner alive but in critical condition and receiving life-saving medical care. The recent spate of harrowingly botched executions across US death penalty states reached a new low late on Wednesday when Tennessee’s governor Bill Lee called off the procedure after Pike had been injected with two full syringes of pentobarbital. She is the only person to have survived being administered 5mg of the sedative – a massive dose that under normal circumstances is considered fatal. Continue reading...

She is the only person to have survived being administered 5mg of the sedative – a massive dose that under normal circumstances is considered fatal. Continue reading...

data.title: You Can See Everything review – Nathan Fielder’s Elizabeth Holmes doc is a modern masterpiece of deceit
data.description: New York film festival: No spoilers here – TV’s grand illusionist meets his match when he moves in with Theranos founder and her family For anyone remotely near the worlds of documentary, comedy or medical fraud, there has been one thing on the mind for weeks now: a single-minute clip of Nathan Fielder , the absurdist comedian whose boundary-pushing HBO series The Rehearsal cemented his status as docu-reality’s premier auteur, staring into the deep blue eyes of Elizabeth Holmes , the disgraced founder of the blood-testing startup Theranos. Unblinking, faces inches apart, the famously dry purveyor of harebrained business schemes and the convicted fraudster appeared locked in a battle of wills. “Are you being real right now?” Fielder asked her, in a classically meta bit – could Fielder really have spent years filming a secret documentary with one of Silicon Valley’s most notorious pariahs? The prospect of TV’s grand illusionist versus emblematic girl-boss scammer seemed potentially too good to be true; buzz for You Can See Everything, Fielder’s furtive documentary co-directed with wunderkind du jour Lance Oppenheim (whose narrative feature debut, the Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime , premiered last month) was such that access to the film’s New York film festival premiere on Wednesday became this fall’s hottest ticket . Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s rational to fear the music industry’: Grouper’s Liz Harris on virality, streaming scammers and her ‘restorative’ dream-pop trio
data.description: When a rarity blew up on TikTok, the solitary ambient artist had fraudsters trying to steal her royalties. It reinforced her DIY mentality – until reforming her band Helen reminded her of the beauty of collaboration In mid-September, I watched as Liz Harris soundchecked to 1,500 empty seats at midtown Manhattan’s historic Town Hall theatre. Soon each plush red chair would be filled for the second of two sold-out nights, but this ornate seclusion felt oddly perfect. It is fair to infer that most of her concertgoers generally listen to the uncanny experimental music she makes as Grouper alone, just as she creates it. Harris started Grouper in 2005 in the DIY noise warehouses of Oakland, California. At 46, she now lives farther north, in coastal Astoria, Oregon, where she creates densely tessellated visual art and spare, lucid albums that have made her a titan of modern ambient music. Painfully beautiful and often inscrutable, hers is a sonic language all its own, creating thickets of sound using little more than guitar or piano, voice and space; her angelic and alien songs have influenced artists as disparate as Phoebe Bridgers and Mk.gee , and been sampled by Lil B and 100 Gecs. It is intensely solitary work, often characterised as sad but full of profound relief. “Like a bloodletting,” Harris offers. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I look at the footage to convince myself that you were alive’: how Ross McElwee made a film about unimaginable loss, grief and guilt
data.description: When his son died aged 27, the director could barely bring himself to watch his old clips of the boy. When at last he did, it was the genesis of an extraordinary project Ross McElwee is the film-maker who spun home movies into art, framing himself and his friends and his son Adrian. The director used to film Adrian for a few minutes each month. He tracked the kid from infancy to adulthood, trying to catch the significant turns of his life. When tragedy struck it back-shadowed the footage. Maybe every home movie is a ghost story at heart. It feels crass to compliment McElwee on his latest documentary, Remake, because it isn’t the picture he’d ever have chosen to make. It is instead a grief-struck tour-de-force: a magnificent film about film-making and its real-world repercussions. McElwee filmed Adrian because he loved him, but now fears he might have hurt him. So he sifts through the material in search of clues, addressing his son as though he’s still in the room. “I look at the footage to convince myself that you were alive,” he says. “But also to convince myself that you’re gone.” Continue reading...

data.description: Israel’s conduct in Gaza shows the danger of using AI in warfare. Humans must remain at the center of wartime decisions As tech leaders warn about the threats of artificial intelligence, most conjure up images of AI agents running amok , such as hacking systems used to run our critical infrastructure, banks or even militaries. Yet one serious danger is mentioned less frequently – the threat posed by AI – empowered lethal weapons. Fully autonomous versions of these weapons are colloquially known as killer robots . Israel’s conduct in Gaza shows that, in an important respect, such AI weapon systems are already here. An algorithm has been deciding who lives and who dies . Continue reading...

data.title: Why boxing is still a box-office smash hit even as the sport’s popularity wanes | Emma John
data.description: Fighters have always provided rich material for stories on stage and screen and the appeal to audiences has not wavered Three of my greatest joys in life are watching sport, going to the theatre and playing violin. So it felt almost embarrassing to discover a classic play that combined all three, yet I’d never heard of it before. To be fair, Golden Boy has not been performed in the UK in more than 40 years and its curious premise may be one of the reasons. Written in 1937, it’s about a gifted young violinist in Depression-era America who also has a talent for boxing and is lured away from music by the pursuit of fame and money in the ring. In the current London production he is played by Josh O’Connor, who Knives Out fans have seen with his fists up as a boxer turned priest in Wake Up Dead Man . O’Connor is no less convincing on stage than on film, attacking a heavy bag with the kind of power that does indeed make you worry for his precious hands. Nor is that ab definition entirely the work of a makeup artist. Continue reading...

data.title: Christa Pike survived her execution attempt. Tennessee must not try again | Austin Sarat
data.description: What happened to Pike was gruesome. No one deserves what she went through, not even those who commit horrible crimes Botched executions are nothing new in US history . In the era when hangings were common, some condemned people were decapitated. Later, when the electric chair was in vogue, every now and again, someone would catch fire during an electrocution. And nitrogen hypoxia, the US’s newest execution method, has already proven notoriously unreliable . But, of all of the ways we have tried to execute people, lethal injection has the worst track record. More than 8% of all lethal injection executions have been botched . Most of them resulted when those charged with carrying them out could not find a usable vein. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Grenfell prosecutions: at last, survivors have a date | Editorial
data.description: Prosecutors will decide who to charge within eight months. But ministers should also re-examine the law Police have at last asked prosecutors to consider charges relating to the Grenfell Tower fire in 2017. The suffering of those who survived or were bereaved by the blaze, which killed 72 people, has been exacerbated by the extraordinary length of time that the investigation has taken. But they can now look forward to a decision about who will face criminal charges. The Crown Prosecution Service has promised that this will be before the 10th anniversary next June. The names of the 20 organisations and 54 individuals in the police files will not be released by prosecutors unless they are charged. But the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and Kensington and Chelsea council have both announced that they are on the list. Angela Rayner promised on Wednesday that the government would cooperate fully whatever decision is reached regarding a potential breach of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 . Kensington and Chelsea council revealed that a charge of corporate manslaughter against it is being considered alongside health and safety and fire regulation breaches. data.title: The Guardian view on the death penalty: Christa Pike’s execution was botched, but cruelty is inherent | Editorial
data.description: Three-quarters of nations have rightly abolished capital punishment in law or practice, but killing by the state has surged in the US What is the kindest way to kill? That’s the question being asked once more following Tennessee’s failed attempts to execute Christa Pike for the brutal murder of a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, when she was 18. The 50-year-old was taken to a medical facility, her condition unknown, with witnesses describing her snoring loudly around 40 minutes after receiving two injections of pentobarbital on Wednesday. It is the second botched killing in months, prompting Tennessee’s governor to order a halt to executions. Lethal injection was supposed to be the humane alternative to firing squads and electric chairs. They in turn were seen as an improvement on hanging, which looked much like lynching in a system disproportionately handing the death penalty to black men. The age and ill health of those executed, and the ethical refusal of most medical staff to be involved, may contribute to botched injections. But analysis of autopsy results has provided compelling evidence that suffering is inherent; injections – especially those involving paralytic drugs – have merely disguised it. What is described as safeguarding the dignity of prisoners is really about reducing the discomfort of witnesses who would otherwise see their suffering. data.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway
data.description: On a night when Erling Haaland moped around the pitch, dragging his hulking frame across the Cardiff turf, Wales registered a welcome victory over 10-man Norway and their first this year. Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind ? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience. “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore,” was the chant aimed at Haaland from the locals. Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb’s well-worked opener in the first half and 17 seconds after the restart Torbjørn Heggem was sent off for fouling James as the Leeds winger streamed towards goal, resulting in a free-kick from which Neco Williams earned Craig Bellamy a timely win with an unerring strike. data.title: Clay Travis: inside the Maga permadad’s world of sports betting, trans panic and more sports betting
data.description: The rightwing media mogul has lost ground to fellow sports bros like Pat McAfee and Joe Rogan. He’s hoping his new venture can recapture some ground When Maga media blowhard Clay Travis offered $2m to Colin Kaepernick last week to appear on the daily talkshow he hosts with former CIA analyst Buck Sexton, it represented the culmination of a years-long obsession on the right with the onetime NFL star. In Travis’s telling of history, Kaepernick taking a knee during the 2016 NFL season was the event that catalyzed professional sports into the era of “woke” excess from which, he claims, it has been struggling to recover ever since. But more than simply confirming the right’s longstanding villainization of Kaepernick, Travis’s offer was also a smarmy bid for publicity for his new media venture, Sport & State. Sport & State, which launched in August, is Travis’s bid to get back to his roots as a media mogul who sold the wildly popular Outkick to Fox Sports for a rumored $100m, and reclaim some of the cultural territory lost to fellow sports bros and Magagitators like Pat McAfee, Joe Rogan, Tucker Carlson and Ben Shapiro. But if there’s one thing Sport & State won’t be doing, it’s engaging with anyone beyond the Magaverse. There has been no response from Kaepernick since Travis made his “offer” of $2m to charity in exchange for an interview, which suggests he understands that it was extended more in a spirit of trolling buffoonery than sincerity. No one associated with the left or progressive politics ever appears on Travis’s shows, for the simple reason that they are designed purely for the right to talk to itself. (Some would say the same could be said of the left, although the disregard for dissenting perspectives in the Magasphere seems way more extreme.) More than it heralds a renewal of Travis’s career or an injection of fresh energy into the Trumpist mediasphere, Sport & State is a case study in the stagnation that has taken hold on the right as Donald Trump stares down the barrel of defeat in November’s midterm elections. Continue reading...

data.title: Uzbekistan dominates chess Olympiad while England’s Sivanandan, 11, sets new world age record
data.description: Host nation won having led almost from start to finish, while young English player reached a stunning landmark Uzbekistan, the host nation, won the open gold medals at the 2026 Olympiad, the biennial chess international team tournament, at Samarkand last week in the style of the legendary Soviet grandmasters of long ago. India, the defending champions, were second, Germany a surprise third, and the top-seeded United States fourth. The hosts led almost from start to finish, with world No 5 Nodirbek Abdusattorov and the world title challenger Javokhir Sindarov their top-board powerhouses. The team recovered swiftly from a single defeat by Germany, and were particularly impressive in crushing Armenia by 3.5-0.5 in the penultimate round. The Uzbekistan government rewarded each of the five players with $200,000 (£178,000), a house and a Volkswagen, plus $50,000 for the coach Rustam Kasimdzhanov. Continue reading...

data.title: US datacenter discharged large amounts of pollution for almost a year with no permits
data.description: Records show Vineland facility in New Jersey emitted health-harming pollution before regulators stepped in DataOne, the Microsoft-linked New Jersey datacenter recently hit with a $1m fine for running unpermitted generators, emitted large amounts of health-harming air pollution for nearly a year before state regulators stepped in, according to public records obtained by Floodlight. The Vineland facility’s 62 gas-fired generators became public in August after a Floodlight/Guardian visual investigation found them operating without permits. The New Jersey department of environmental protection last week fined the company over the fleet but did not disclose how long the generators had been operating nor how much air pollution they had released into the surrounding community over the past year. data.title: Kill Jackie review – Catherine Zeta-Jones’ assassin thriller is like Killing Eve … minus good characters or plot
data.description: This preposterous nonsense probably had high intentions – and then realised it’s easier to replace credible writing with gunfights, car chases and ear-bitings A freeport is somewhere you can store imported goods and not have to pay any of the duties usually required by the bothersome authorities until you move them out of there. It’s not quite what I expected to learn when watching a new crime-caper-comedy-thriller-cum-comeback-vehicle starring Catherine Zeta-Jones, but on the other hand I didn’t expect to learn anything at all so we could consider it a bonus. The customs benefits and tax reliefs available in certain exclusionary zones are the carefully explained means by which Jackie Price (Zeta-Jones) has established a successful art business over the last 20 years. She acquires art, puts it in a warehouse, invites rich people to come and view it, bid on it and buy it. I don’t know if they bear the cost of the taxes themselves as they ship it home, or indeed whether this is included in the bid price or not. Having been led by the early scenes to believe there would be much more in the way of financial detail, I now find myself beset by questions. Continue reading...

data.title: A new Skywalker trilogy for Star Wars? Going back to the same family-saga well is a waste of time
data.description: Reports that Jon Watts could make a new trilogy about a clan who have already saved and destroyed the galaxy several times over leaves you wishing for a newer world The Skywalkers: who are they exactly? A family that has moulded the entire Star Wars galaxy in their image, to the extent that nobody can really imagine the long-running space opera without them. An almost endless familial battle between good and evil, featuring absent fathers, secret siblings, murdered mentors, wayward nephews, surprise grandfathers. For nearly half a century they have blown up Death Stars, built Death Stars, destroyed Jedi orders, rebuilt Jedi orders, fallen to the dark side, risen from the dark side, died heroically, come back as ghosts. Star Wars has occasionally attempted to escape them. It has made films and TV shows about stolen Death Star plans, bounty hunters, smugglers and rebels from entirely different corners of the galaxy. Ryan Gosling will soon appear in a Star Wars movie that, as far as we know, has absolutely nothing to do with them. But they have never really gone away, and now they are back, possibly because Disney has run out of ideas for how to take the franchise forward without them. Deadline reports this week that Lucasfilm has hired Jon Watts to direct the first instalment of a new trilogy continuing the Skywalker saga, written by Simon Kinberg, with Daisy Ridley reportedly being eyed to return as Rey. The films have not yet been greenlit, and there are precious few other details, but Watts does seem an inspired choice, if for no other reason than that he has previously overseen a film – Spider-Man: No Way Home – that was built around the idea that nobody in a long-running franchise needs to remain dead. data.translatedTitle: A new Skywalker trilogy for Star Wars? Going back to the same family-saga well is a waste of time
data.translatedDescription: Reports that Jon Watts could make a new trilogy about a clan who have already saved and destroyed the galaxy several times over leaves you wishing for a newer world The Skywalkers: who are they exactly? A family that has moulded the entire Star Wars galaxy in their image, to the extent that nobody can really imagine the long-running space opera without them. An almost endless familial battle between good and evil, featuring absent fathers, secret siblings, murdered mentors, wayward nephews, surprise grandfathers. For nearly half a century they have blown up Death Stars, built Death Stars, destroyed Jedi orders, rebuilt Jedi orders, fallen to the dark side, risen from the dark side, died heroically, come back as ghosts. Star Wars has occasionally attempted to escape them. It has made films and TV shows about stolen Death Star plans, bounty hunters, smugglers and rebels from entirely different corners of the galaxy. Ryan Gosling will soon appear in a Star Wars movie that, as far as we know, has absolutely nothing to do with them. But they have never really gone away, and now they are back, possibly because Disney has run out of ideas for how to take the franchise forward without them. Deadline reports this week that Lucasfilm has hired Jon Watts to direct the first instalment of a new trilogy continuing the Skywalker saga, written by Simon Kinberg, with Daisy Ridley reportedly being eyed to return as Rey. The films have not yet been greenlit, and there are precious few other details, but Watts does seem an inspired choice, if for no other reason than that he has previously overseen a film – Spider-Man: No Way Home – that was built around the idea that nobody in a long-running franchise needs to remain dead. data.title: Take It or Leave It review – vividly atmospheric formative adventures of future pop princes Madness
data.description: Docufictional 1981 comedy captures the working-class ska-pop pranksters in their hungry years with an almost Loachian authenticity Opting for the former is the best idea for this unexpectedly revealing, vividly atmospheric, often funny and alarming, docufictional comedy from 1981 about the rise of the baggy-trousered ska-pop national treasures Madness. It takes us from their beginnings in 1976 to their chart breakthrough: gormless, penniless blokes, obsessing about music and roaming north London’s gritty districts of Camden Town, Stoke Newington and Crouch End. (This elicits some droll dialogue: “They’re all the same, these streets” … “That’s why they put signs on them.”) Our naughty, dodgy heroes play people’s parties, sign on the dole and do mortifying odd jobs, get told off by site foremen and office supervisors, drive to gigs in Arthur Daley vans, almost get into fights with skinheads and have calamitous arguments with the drummer during rehearsals. It could have carried on like that indefinitely, but the arrival of Graham “Suggs” McPherson as singer is the mysterious ingredient around which everything coalesces: his voice miraculously ups the band’s game, apparently curing their worrying propensity for playing flat. His vocals mesh with the reggae thump of the keyboards and sax and the rest of the band’s goofy jogging-on-the-spot stage energy. Continue reading...

data.title: Get Jiro to Below: the seven best shows to stream this week
data.description: A sushi master seeks bloody revenge in Anthony Bourdain’s hilariously gory dystopian animation, while Josh Hartnett’s Jaws-esque horror about a mystery sea creature terrorising a small town will keep you guessing all the way Anthony Bourdain’s eccentric, epicurean spirit lives on through this animation, adapted from a graphic novel series he created with Joel Rose. It’s set in a lawless, near-future LA where food is the only non-digital pleasure left. No one is more important than chefs. Our hero, sushi master Jiro, languishes in the projects with only embattled mother Miyako and sharp knives for company. When he upsets some mobsters, a survival battle ensues. Cue a series of hilariously gory deaths (one man is executed using hollandaise sauce) and lavish celebrations of food culture. The story is hokey and the dialogue doesn’t always sing but Bourdain’s love of food as a sensory delight is greedily indulged. HBO Max, from Sunday 4 October Continue reading...

data.title: Greg Freeman: All Set the Bone review – ambitious alt-country double album spreads its talents a touch thin
data.description: (Transgressive) The Maryland singer-songwriter’s third album has an impressive sense of scale compared to last year’s breakout Burnover, but is less immediately appealing Greg Freeman’s third album All Set the Bone feels, at its best and most nervy, like an off-brand pressure cooker: too hot, bursting at its seams, rattling with kinetic energy. The Maryland-born singer-songwriter has a voice that often sounds like it’s straining at its limits, and although he is ostensibly part of a growing indierock revival that’s been taking hold over the past few years – a cosy perennial – there’s nothing particularly comfortable about the songs on this double album. On Marooned, frantic stabs of guitar and drums create queasy unease; opener Cahokia muddles up the catharsis of a great American road song, descending into proggy bedlam. And his lyrics most often drum up anxieties big and small: “Who do you look to when you’re all on your own?” he asks on Culture. “When all your heroes lost their microphones?” Freeman broke out with last year’s Burnover , a set of taut story-songs that were at turns witty, delirious and devastating. Freeman’s secret was in his ability to weld that literary streak to loud, bolshy, riff-heavy music that wouldn’t sound out of place on mainstream rock radio. All Set the Bone is several orders more ambitious in its scale, and its songwriting, which is more imagistic and diffuse. The result is an impressive record but one that’s less immediately appealing. Freeman wrote it while travelling through the US and reckoning with “a lot of change in my personal sense of … everything”, and you can hear that searching quality in the final product. All Set the Bone contains fewer fireworks than Burnover, but Freeman still has plenty of spark. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Shane was rascality personified’: the Pogues on their late frontman, anti-Irish prejudice and the feud over Fairytale of New York
data.description: The Celtic punk band’s co-founders Spider Stacy and James Fearnley take your questions about Shane MacGowan, ruffling the feathers of trad musicians and putting Laurence Fox in his place The Pogues earned a reputation early on as a ferocious live band. What does it feel like to be in the middle of that whirlwind? VerulamiumParkRanger Spider Stacy [co-founder, tin whistle, vocals]: Last Christmas, we did a secret gig in a pub in Nunhead [in London] and it reminded me of those early days when we were so close to the audience, who were practically on top of each other. The venue that most sticks in my mind is the Hope & Anchor [in Islington, London]. We played there to about 35 people [in 1983], but when we went back a month later the match had been struck and it was absolutely roaring. data.title: Trá Pháidín: Cloch’s Claí review – giddy Galway gang burst the boundaries of folk music
data.description: (World of Echo) With musical ideas spanning mariachi and motorik beats, and lyrics with Kneecap-grade rage, this brilliant collective evolve tradition with stinging, joyful songs Quicksilver and giddy in its exploration of Irish music, language and identity, Trá Pháidín’s second album bursts open the idea of a 21st-century traditional folk record. It woos you with the reverb-smothered guitars and birdsong-like flutes of Tí Mhichael Phaddy (Michael Paddy’s House, an opener suggesting a psychedelically perfect rurality) before an Irish woman cuts in, bigging up her countryside Airbnb on the phone. A shouty local then comically interrupts her. Trá Pháidín (Paddy’s Beach) are a six-strong collective of brilliant musicians from Galway, Ireland’s largest Irish-speaking county, and their album’s title, Cloch’s Claí (Stone and Dry Stone Wall), suggests that each track plays its own scabrous, weight-bearing part in the whole. The 45 minutes unfold as an interrupted sequence, full of improvisation, texture and ornament, the band freely roaming other genres, revealing them as connected neighbourhoods. Continue reading...

data.title: Geneva Lewis: Barber, Zorn, Glass album review – virtuosity and warmth
data.description: Lewis/BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra/New (Delos) The young New Zealand violinist has chosen an all-American programme for her label debut, and impresses with works by Barber, Zorn and Glass A former BBC New Generation Artist, violinist Geneva Lewis has chosen an all-American program for her Delos recording debut. She’s accompanied with palpable empathy by fellow New Zealander Gemma New conducting the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra. Samuel Barber’s concerto receives an airy, poetic reading with Lewis and New embracing the music’s lyrical pastoralism while pointing up the opening movement’s scotch snap. The ongoing Celtic motif is seized upon by the orchestra and pays off in a moto perpetuo conclusion that feels second cousin to a highland fling. Lewis’s tone is warm and full of feeling, aching in the allegro and andante, feisty and folkish in the finale. Continue reading...

data.title: Rhapsody: A Manifesto by Alice Oswald review – a history of the spoken word, from Homer to Ted Hughes
data.description: A twisting, beguiling investigation into the art of poetry that ends in a call to arms on behalf of the natural world The poet Alice Oswald is no stranger to thinking in public about her art. She was Oxford professor of poetry until 2023, and her lectures are available online. But this is her first full-length book, and as such is something of an occasion. So what exactly is it? For a work of prose it contains a lot of poetry, much translated or composed by Oswald herself. Shakespeare, Donne, Shelley and Ted Hughes also feature. Though nonfiction, the book is full of stories, particularly retellings of Homer and Aeschylus. It is billed as “genre-defying” and there is much formal experimentation. But at heart it is an exploration of the oral tradition, and the writer’s own subtitle is A Manifesto, which feels exciting and urgent, pointed at the contemporary world with its pressing realities. Continue reading...

data.title: What we’re reading: China Miéville, Sebastian Barry, Derek Owusu and Guardian readers on the books they enjoyed in September
data.description: Writers and Guardian readers discuss the titles they have read over the last month. Join the conversation in the comments I was sideswiped by Giada Scodellaro’s Ruins, Child . A brilliant, strange book that challenged me in the most exhilarating way, with its fractured language and dream-cinema visions, the sense it bestowed of walking through a corridor full of echoes. Echoes of a less elliptical but no-less political kind haunt Jordy Rosenberg’s astounding Night Night Fawn . I guess you could call it a family novel? But it’s at least as much about fascism as it is about the family – as well as about unsettling linkages between the two. And for horrors and rage in a nonfiction register, Jonas Marvin’s The Breaking of the English Working Class is an indispensable – and beautifully written – essay on decades of structural, economic and psychic violence. The feeling it provoked in me brought to mind John Berger’s phrase “undefeated despair”. Continue reading...

data.description: This wry debut novel about a male model’s inner life, written in lowercase fragments, has tender insights but isn’t as profound as it aims to be Should you care about a vape-loving, philandering male model who just goes with the flow because that’s life? Yes, says The Long Cloud, the wry debut novel of New Zealand artist and photographer Hector MacKenzie. Is it convincing? Well, sort of. Xander, a 30-year-old former jock ageing out of the modelling industry and into an existential crisis, is a tabula rasa of sorts – a way for readers to glimpse reflections of themselves. data.title: Gears of War: E-Day review – an alien invasion shouldn’t be this boring
data.description: Xbox, PC (version tested); The Coalition/Xbox Game Studios E-Day boasts the best combat in 20 years of Gears games – but everything surrounding it is disappointing Every Gears of War game released in the last 20 years has made reverent reference to Emergence Day, when alien creatures emerged from the earth, single-minded in their savagery. In E-Day, you’re there to witness it: the police lights, flipped cars, ground tremors, civilians running, aliens pouring out of fissures in the earth and ripping faces off. You’re at ground zero in a squad of four soldiers called Gears – Marcus Fenix, the leader; Dom, who wants to retire; Lucas, a green cadet with a buzzcut; and the dishonourably discharged Mags. Only this dysfunctional quartet can turn the tide. With guns. Lots of ’em. Instead of answering questions raised by the ending of 2019’s Gears 5 , we’re back to the start to find out why Marcus has a scar on his lip and why these soldiers started strapping chainsaws on to their assault rifles. Anything that was left to the imagination is here, for you to point at and say: “I understood that reference. This is a thing that I have seen.” Continue reading...

data.title: The ICE documentary as chilling as a horror movie: ‘We’re trying to put the audience in a position of terror’
data.description: Film-makers Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller’s new short is an unvarnished portrait of ICE-occupied Minneapolis Get Out . The Texas Chainsaw Massacre . The Purge . All three films build on an august tradition of using horror as a Trojan horse to comment on the social, political and racial anxieties of their day. They’re Here, a new documentary featured in this year’s New York film festival , flips the script. Directed by Rachel Lauren Mueller , a journalist, and Laura Poitras , Academy award-winner, the 24-minute film employs horror tropes to re-examine the surge of Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) offiers in Minneapolis last winter. “For filmmakers and journalists, there’s a great sense of responsibility in these moments when they arise,” said Mueller, a Minneapolis resident. “This is my neighborhood. It was my community. It was very clear to me what my role in this moment would be.” Framed as a dystopian story set in an urban tundra, They’re Here follows the Trump administration’s border control campaign in Minnesota – officially dubbed Operation Metro Surge . Over the course of three winter months, the Department of Homeland Security moved to remove the Twin Cities’ Somali immigrant population and destabilize its progressive political order. The documentary takes in the wanton shock-and-awe campaign and scales it down to the battlefield, following Minneapolis residents as they evade and resist ICE and customs and border patrol agents – obscuring the residents’ identities for protection. Continue reading...

data.title: Hay Fever review – Richard E Grant and Christine Baranski host Coward’s country house shenanigans
data.description: Wyndham’s theatre, London Grant brings shock-haired vigour as a vain novelist forced to welcome his boho children’s surprise guests in comedy of clipped social embarrassment Hay Fever, now one of Noël Coward’s best-known and most-performed works, hasn’t always been a smash hit. British critics who found its West End debut in 1925 amusing enough nevertheless noted its lack of plot, and the first Broadway production was a flop. A critic for Vogue called it “funny in places”, which sounds like the kind of stinging putdown you’d expect from the playwright’s own hand. A century of performances have proved the play’s lasting power, but its comic effect has always lain less in the words as written than their delivery – it is, after all, about a family that is “artificial to the point of lunacy”. At their centre is diva Judith Bliss, who has retired from the stage to take up the role of country hostess. When she, her husband and their self-consciously bohemian children Sorel and Simon all invite surprise guests for the weekend, the unfortunate attendees find themselves embroiled in a self-serving drama of exquisite embarrassment. Continue reading...

data.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for flourless walnut, date and espresso cake | The sweet spot
data.description: With a deep, caramel richness and a bitter undertone, this cake is an excellent addition to your home baking roster There’s enough dark chocolate in this gluten-free cake to put it firmly in chocolate cake territory, but the hero flavour comes from the sweet, creamy nuttiness of walnuts, so it’s important to use very fresh ones, because stale walnuts can quickly turn bitter. The dates bring a deep, caramel richness, while the espresso pulls everything back from being overly sweet. Despite all that richness, the cake is wonderfully light in texture. Serve with creme fraiche and perhaps some poached pears, if you want to turn it into a full-blown dessert. Continue reading...

data.title: The best dishes to come out of a roasting tin
data.description: Baked pasta, gnocchi, chicken, meatballs and greens – all perfectly served straight from the oven • Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast As I have mentioned before, we live directly above a takeaway pizzeria and tavola calda (a canteen-like spot that translates as “hot table”). My desk is by the window, so the writing and editing of my next book (a collection of regional recipes that is only two years late) has been accompanied by the smell of whatever is cooking in their kitchen downstairs, before being arranged, in big roasting trays, behind a glass counter. Occasionally, I have to shut the window, but mostly the steady stream of pizza, baked pasta, braised meat, meatballs, roast potatoes and green vegetables shining with olive oil inspires me. And that is the inspiration for this newsletter: ideas for easygoing dishes that are best served straight from their rectangular roasting tins. As I write this, it is almost lunchtime, so, driven by my own hunger, I would like the first serving from a roasting tray to be Angela Hartnett’s macaroni cheese : al dente pasta mixed with béchamel and various cheeses, then baked until golden brown and bubbling at the edges. Just as welcome would be a plate of baked pasta inspired by one of my friend Cinzia’s dishes: meze maniche, rigatoni, penne or macaroni with a rich tomato sauce, basil, lots of mozzarella and pecorino. Or a slice of Meera Sodha’s vegan sweet potato, miso and wholemeal lasagne , which, she promises, takes 15 minutes to put together and uses good, flavourful, ready-made ingredients such as miso, sun-dried tomato paste and passata. Continue reading...

data.title: From breakfast pancakes to dinner sides and pudding: Alissa Timoshkina’s apple recipes
data.description: Fried in pancakes, braised with duck, pickled with a roast chicken or baked for pudding, apples are one of autumn’s star ingredients Few ingredients are as familiar as apples, yet few carry such symbolic weight. Peaking just as the season’s begin to turn, they are the ultimate symbol of nature’s abundance, imbued with a sense of nostalgia for the retreating sunlight. The symbolism became unexpectedly tangible to me during a recent autumn apple-picking trip with my family: surrounded by branches heavy with fruit, I found myself seeing the humble apple with fresh awe. It looked nothing short of nature’s miracle. Native to the mountains of central Asia, near the modern Kazakhstan-China border, it has travelled further than perhaps any other fruit, becoming at home in cuisines from Normandy to New York, Caucasus to Kashmir. Sweet or savoury, everyday or celebratory, the apple is truly universal. Its versatility always reminds me of the simple joy of cooking with the seasons. Continue reading...

data.title: My wife obsessively consumes US news. She’s so stressed but can’t turn off. What should I do? | Leading questions
data.description: Instead of asking her to step away from her distress, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith , could you suggest she channel it into action? Read more Leading questions My wife is obsessed with everything that’s happening in the US. She literally spends all day sitting on the couch, watching videos and reading opinion pieces. She’s originally from America and has been living abroad for 25 years and she has family in the US, so I get that she needs to feel connected to what’s happening. But it’s constant. Whether we’re eating, watching a TV show or movie, when we’re talking about something completely unrelated – everything, every topic, either starts or ends with outrage. I’ve told her she needs to take at least one day off all social media, but she won’t do that even for an hour. It stresses her out more and more every day, but she just keeps going back to it – and it has been really affecting me, more lately than ever. On weekends I stay up late playing games (my way of winding down after a week of work) and she’ll go to bed early. And during those times sometimes I just sit and cry. Everything that’s happening is so stressful, and there’s nothing we can do about it. I just wish I could rip away her phone and let her breathe! I don’t know what to say or do. Is there anything that could help? Continue reading...

data.title: While I dream of garden greenhouses, a coldframe will do me just fine
data.description: A hothouse in my garden may be just a fantasy, but I can still offer plenty of protection for tender plants I thought I would have had a new coldframe by now, but the only new thing in the garden is a fox hole. It would be more polite of them to direct their exemplary digging skills towards where we’re excavating for new foundations, but so it goes. I’m writing this, then, in the hope that it will spur me on to order one. I like to think that, one day, in a fantasy life, I might be a greenhouse person. I’d fill it up with pelargonium cuttings and orange blossom and hold tiny little lunch parties for one. Or maybe have a clever walk-through one like Mary Keen’s – genius for making sure you go in there, what with it being on the path. But I think of glasshouse life in the same way I think of one day learning Italian. It’s a nice idea, but unlikely to happen. Continue reading...

data.title: Inside the undersea kingdom: the secret, sinister battle to control what lies beneath the waves
data.description: Every day, trillions of dollars, oil and gas and 99% of the world’s web traffic move through undersea pipelines that bear no state’s protection. With superpowers and corporations vying for control, should we be worried about this new wild west? On Christmas Day 2024, six weeks before Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania were due to disconnect themselves from Russia’s power grid, a Finnish engineer was just about to sit down to lunch when his phone rang. He was responsible for the Finnish side of the undersea cables that keep Finland and the Baltic states supplied with electricity, and one was malfunctioning. Within a couple of hours, authorities knew that a Cook Islands-registered tanker called the Eagle S, part of the shadow fleet carrying sanctioned Russian oil, in this case to Egypt, had sailed over the cable at the moment and location at which it had stopped working. The coastguard hailed the Eagle S. Were their anchors up? Yes, they replied – though they did not seem to check – and sailed on. Three hours later the ship hit another four cables in quick succession, nearly hobbling internet provision in Finland and Estonia – and was minutes away from a major electricity cable and the Balticconnector, which supplies the two countries with gas. Finland scrambled the border guard, which pulled up alongside the tanker and demanded the crew take up its anchor. But the Eagle S was not in Finnish territorial waters: the authorities could not force the captain to comply, and they did not know who or what might come to his aid. Continue reading...

data.title: Tell us: what happened after you froze your eggs?
data.description: Much is made of the decision to try to preserve fertility but less explored are the choices that come afterwards. We want to hear from people about what happened next Oocyte cryopreservation, more commonly known as egg freezing, has been around for decades but the procedure stopped being considered experimental in 2012. Since then, elective egg freezing has boomed. Often represented as an insurance policy against age- or illness-related fertility decline, the process can be costly and complex. While figures vary, research suggests most people who undergo egg freezing never access their eggs and results are mixed for those who do. Long-term storage poses its own costs and questions. Continue reading...

data.title: Scientists released fluorescent dye nearly 2 km underwater; it revealed deep water rising 100 metres a day
data.description: Researchers utilized fluorescein dye in the Rockall Trough to study deep ocean water upwelling. They measured rapid upward movement reaching about 125 metres per day, significantly faster than average estimates. This study provides direct observations of upwelling in submarines canyons, offering insights into ocean circulation dynamics. Findings suggest underwater topography plays a crucial role in deep-water circulation processes. Future research aims to explore similar processes in different submarine canyon settings.

data.title: How Paddy McKillen Jr went from king of Irish nightlife to €270 in the bank
data.description: Through his Press Up group, Paddy McKillen Jr built one of Ireland’s biggest hospitality empires, employing thousands of people across dozens of venues. The son of billionaire property developer Paddy McKillen Sr, he appeared to be building a formidable legacy of his own. But last week, the High Court heard he had just €270 in a Revolut account, against liabilities of almost €28 million. So, how did it all unravel, and could he ever build again? Today on The Indo Daily, Fionnán Sheahan is joined by the Irish Independent’s Shane Phelan and John Burns to explore how Paddy McKillen Jr’s business empire came apart, and what might come next. We want to earn your trust and are members of the Trust Project. See our ethics policies at independent.ie/ourjournalism.

data.title: Nova ferramenta de IA prevê rota e intensidade de tempestades em curtíssimo prazo
data.description: Saber com exatidão a rota de uma tempestade e a intensidade da chuva para os próximos 30 minutos deixou de ser um desafio que exige supercomputadores. Uma nova ferramenta -desenvolvida na USP (Universidade de São Paulo ) e denominada TITAN-LSTM- une dados de radares meteorológicos e inteligência artificial para realizar previsões de curtíssimo prazo, rastreando e atualizando o trajeto, a área e a intensidade da precipitação a cada cinco minutos. O sistema se destaca pelo seu baixo custo computacional, o que facilita a sua aplicação em diversas regiões que já contam com cobertura de radares. Leia mais (10/02/2026 - 07h00)

data.title: Highline capta R$ 72,9 milhões com Ministério das Comunicações e BNDES para expansão móvel
data.description: A Highline obteve financiamento de R$ 72,9 milhões para ampliar cobertura móvel de alta capacidade em 131 localidades, entre elas 13 favelas. O dinheiro será do FUST (Fundo de Universalização dos Serviços de Telecomunicações), gerido pelo Ministério das Comunicações e tem o BNDES (Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social) como agente financeiro. As áreas beneficiadas estão no Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, São Paulo, Paraná, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul e Bahia. Leia mais (10/02/2026 - 07h00)

data.title: Bipolares pela democracia
data.description: Carrinho do terror subindo a montanha-russa ! Ventinho na cara como lambidas libidinosas de fadas safadas. Meu cérebro comete poeminhas juvenis. Hálito de Halls de menta com chá de canela. Chá de minhápica. Não consigo parar de pensar em como é bonito o homem quando da barafunda da barba sai um beiço carnudo. É como se aquele beiço fosse um jovem do " Largados e Pelados " no meio da mata, e então ele vence a mata. Vencer a mata. Vencer a morte. Formigamento de prazer do esfíncter até o occipital. Sobe! Postes, batons, desodorantes, caneta de dez cores, maçaneta. Tudo é sexy e tudo é sexo . Neste dia, apenas uma certeza: é preciso novamente votar pela democracia . Leia mais (10/01/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: Supremo manda para conciliação julgamento sobre reajuste de plano de saúde de idosos

Quase 17 milhões de pessoas foram ver "O Guardião do Rei", que narra a amizade improvável entre um rei deposto e um camponês encarregado de vigiá-lo. Com o número impressionante, o longa se tornou o segundo mais visto na história do cinema do país asiático e a maior bilheteria até hoje. Leia mais (10/01/2026 - 19h30)

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Trams att skatt skulle få alla miljardärer att fly landet”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Sverige kan beskatta sina miljardärer. Tesen att de alla skulle fly landet har redan prövats – både här och i Norge. Visst skedde en utflyttning. data.title: Insändare. Svar: Arbetsförmedlare kanske ska tvingas sänka sin lön
data.description: SVAR PÅ INSÄNDARE. Det är tydligt att Arbetsförmedlingen inte har koll på behovet av anställda i många yrken, till exempel undersköterskor. Kanske ska anställda på Arbetsförmedlingen i likhet med arbetslösa tvingas minska lönen med 5 procent för var hundrade dag om de inte får fram jobb till arbetslösa, skriver Niclas Lundberg.

data.title: De koning wilde weten wát zijn voorouders deden in de koloniën – nu krijgt hij antwoord
data.description: Deze vrijdag verschijnt een „allesomvattend” onderzoek over welke rol het Huis Oranje-Nassau speelde in de koloniale geschiedenis. data.title: Europejska motoryzacja zapatrzyła się w ekrany. Rimac radzi spojrzeć na zegarek

data.title: Do klečících lidí ve svatyni najelo auto v plné rychlosti. Řidič přiznal fatální omyl
data.description: Velkou pozornost na sociálních sítích sbírá video z thajského Bangkoku. Do areálu svatyně Guanyin totiž nečekaně vjelo auto a narazilo do lidí před oltářem. data.title: U klatovského letiště zemřel parašutista, padal z výšky několika kilometrů
data.description: Všechny složky záchranného systému zasahovaly v pátek dopoledne u letiště v Klatovech. Podle dostupných informací se tam při pádu zranil jednapadesátiletý parašutista. Jeho zranění byla ale natolik vážná, že mu zdravotničtí záchranáři již nedokázali pomoct.

data.title: Pavel s první dámou vyprávějí o pejskovi a kočičce. Udělejte si čas na čtení, vyzývají
data.description: Prezident Petr Pavel a první dáma Eva Pavlová se zapojili do Týdne čtení dětem. Na sociálních sítích sdíleli video, ve kterém společně předčítají příběh Josefa Čapka o tom, jak pejsek s kočičkou pekli dort. Dospělé vyzvali, aby si čas na čtení našli po celý rok.

data.title: Při nehodě v americkém Wyomingu zemřeli dva Češi, další je zraněný
data.description: Při dopravní nehodě v americkém státě Wyoming zemřeli dva čeští občané, další Čech byl zraněn, sdělil mluvčí ministerstva zahraničí Adam Čörgő. Případem se podle něj zabývá český generální konzulát v Los Angeles.

data.title: Turek se omluvil Hnutí Duha za výrok o parazitech. Satisfakce, reagoval spolek
data.description: Poslanec za Motoristy sobě Filip Turek se omluvil neziskové organizaci Hnutí Duha za to, že je označil za parazity. Turek v omluvě zmínil, že jeho tehdejší výrok se nezakládal na pravdě a byl neoprávněným zásahem do pověsti spolku. Ekologická organizace podala žalobu na konci června rovněž kvůli tomu, že ji čestný prezident Motoristů spojoval s úmrtími při povodních na podzim v roce 2024.

data.title: Řidič špatně zapojil tažné zařízení, přívěs s naloženým autem utopil v rybníku
data.description: O velké smůle může mluvit řidič, který ve čtvrtek na Šumpersku převážel na přívěsu osobní auto. Nedostatečně totiž upevnil tažné zařízení a to upadlo zrovna ve chvíli, kdy jel kolem rybníka, v němž následně skončil převrácený přívěs i s jeho nákladem.

data.title: Jak se liší BIO maso od běžného? Rozhodují pastviny, krmivo i léčba
data.description: Když se řekne ekologický chov, mnozí si představí krávy pasoucí se na louce. Přístup k venkovnímu prostoru a možnost přirozeného pohybu patří mezi principy ekologického zemědělství, ale za BIO certifikací stojí mnohem víc než jen hezký pohled na zvířata na pastvě. Co musí splnit farma, která chce své maso, mléko nebo vejce prodávat jako ekologické?

data.title: Mám to pod kontrolou. Vraky aut po Praze upozorňují řidiče na chyby za volantem
data.description: Pohled do telefonu, nedostatečný odstup, rychlá jízda nebo jen chvilka nepozornosti. To vše může mít fatální následek pro jednotlivce i okolí. Kampaň v centru Prahy, kde hlavní roli hrají vraky aut, upozorňuje řidiče, že je vždy lépe věnovat řízení plnou pozornost. Instalace vraků lze najít na čtyřech vytížených místech metropole.

data.title: Cesta na Island i termín u lékaře. Část opozice vynechala hlasování o nedůvěře
data.description: Vláda Andreje Babiše ve čtvrtek hladce udržela důvěru Poslanecké sněmovny, od začátku bylo jasné, že opozice nemá dost hlasů proti. Současnému kabinetu však pomohla taky absence devíti opozičních poslanců. Ti podle svých slov byli v zahraničí, někteří chyběli kvůli rodinným či zdravotním důvodům. Například poslankyně ODS Renáta Zajíčková byla na dlouho připravované cestě na Island.

data.title: Trump chce uchránit Oválnou pracovnu od demolice. Jeho zlaté úpravy mají zůstat
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump prohlásil, že mu Tajná služba doporučila zbourat Oválnou pracovnu v Bílém domě a postavit novou. Návrh vyloučil s tím, že naopak hledá způsob, jak trvale uchovat změny, které v místnosti během svého mandátu prosadil – včetně nepřehlédnutelné zlaté výzdoby.

data.title: Nález těla u skládky ve Frýdku-Místku. Policie zjišťuje, zda jde o ztracenou ženu
data.description: Bezmála měsíční pátrání po osmatřicetileté Janě Šerjeníkové z Frýdku-Místku je možná u konce. Podle neoficiálních informací našla policie tělo v rozkladu v lese u skládky. Policie totožnost zatím nepotvrdila, dnes by však měla k případu zveřejnit nové informace.

data.title: Rusové se zaměřili na klíčový most v Kyjevě, Ukrajinci zasáhli rafinerii ve Volgogradu
data.description: Ukrajinská armáda v noci na pátek podnikla rozsáhlý dronový útok na průmyslovou infrastrukturu ve Volgogradské oblasti. Jeden z dronů způsobil požár ve výškovém obytném domě ve Volgogradu. Ruská armáda zato znovu zaútočila na Jižní most v Kyjevě, přes který vede důležitý silniční tah i trasa metra, na jiném místě při ruském náletu zemřel jeden člověk.

data.title: Zakopl před královnou, nepoznal Bushe. Havlův dvorní fotograf vzpomíná
data.description: „Existuje něco jako ne-náhoda. Osud, chcete-li,“ uvažuje v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz Tomki Němec. Ve svých šestadvaceti letech se stal osobním fotografem Václava Havla. Během porevolučních let s ním navštívil Bílý dům, Elysejský palác i Downing Street. K jeho nedožitým devadesátinám nyní vydává knihu fotografií a znovu otevírá téma poněkud nekonvenčního prezidenta.

data.title: Dlouhý provaz z vraků. Americkou dálnici zablokovala v mlze obří hromadná nehoda
data.description: Přes šedesát řidičů ve čtvrtek havarovalo na americké dálnici I-95 v Jižní Karolíně. Nejméně jedenáct lidí utrpělo zranění, záchranné služby je museli ošetřit na nejbližší hasičské stanici. Jednoho člověka vrtulník transportoval do nemocnice, podrobnosti o jeho stavu zatím nejsou známé. Nehodu mohla zapříčinit hustá mlha.

data.title: Parkovné nemá být daň městu za vlastnictví auta, říká olomoucký lídr ODS
data.description: Po minulých komunálních volbách skončila ODS v olomouckém zastupitelstvu poprvé od roku 2002 v opozici. Zpět do koaličních lavic by ji měl nyní přivést podnikatel Jan Vašíř, zástupce nové mladé generace občanských demokratů. „Byli bychom rádi, kdyby Olomouc byla atraktivním městem pro mladé lidi, současně zde však ti starší musí nalézt všechny služby, jež ve svém věku potřebují,“ říká.

data.title: Dvakrát Cave, Morcheeba či Alanis. Jaké hvězdy přivezl končící festival Metronome
data.description: Letošním ročníkem se rozloučil hudební festival Metronome Prague. Za deset let jeho trvání přivezli pořadatelé do Prahy hned několik zahraničních hudebních hvězd. data.title: Vysychající Lipno odhalilo náhrobky, vorový kanál i staré nádraží
data.description: Lipno je plné už jen z poloviny a voda se „ztrácí“ dál. Zatím vydatně neprší a ani předpovědi nejsou příliš optimistické. Vydali jsme se proto s fotoaparátem na různá místa lipenské přehrady, která jsou běžně zatopená. Fotoreportér iDNES.cz našel staré nádraží, vorový kanál i náhrobky.

data.title: Jsme opozicí, kterou by si mohla přát každá koalice, říká lídr hnutí Zlín 21
data.description: Hnutí Zlín 21 získalo v posledních komunálních volbách 17 procent hlasů. O čtyři roky dříve to bylo 15 procent. Navzdory těmto výsledkům skončilo vždy v opozici. Letos to chce prolomit a stát se konečně součástí koalice, která řídí město. Do voleb ho opět vede jako lídr podnikatel a zastupitel Čestmír Vančura, který je i jeho předsedou.

data.title: „V koalici to nefunguje.“ Lídr ODS Soukup kritizuje zásady pro developery i kasárna
data.description: Když už se Martin Soukup zvolna chystal do politického důchodu, zasáhla do jeho plánů nešťastná událost, která jej donutila vše přehodnotit. Úmrtí hradeckého exprimátora Oldřicha Vlasáka, od něhož uplynou dva roky, otevřelo Soukupovi neplánovaně dveře do městské rady. Stal se nejen předsedou výboru pro územní plánování, ale především velkým kritikem fungování koalice, do které jeho ODS patří.

data.description: Výstava v pražské Písecké bráně Co je za obrazem? uvede k nedožitým 90. narozeninám díla ze sbírky režiséra, herce, pedagoga a spisovatele Jana Kačera. data.title: Chceme lidem usnadňovat život, říká lídr ODS Tichý. Je proti novému magistrátu
data.description: Před čtyřmi lety šla ODS do voleb v Pardubicích pod hlavičkou koalice SPOLU. A i když zaznamenala druhý nejlepší výsledek, nakonec skončila v opozici. Možná i proto letos ODS vsadila na některé neokoukané tváře. On Saturday, Oct. 24, all four will step into the Octagon at Etihad Arena on Yas Island as UFC 333: Volkanovski vs. Evloev brings two championship fights to Abu Dhabi.

data.title: Droits humains au Burundi : Un autre rapport de Zongo contesté
data.description:
Gitega rejette le rapport de Fortuné Gaëtan Zongo, Rapporteur spécial des Nations-unies sur la situation des humains au Burundi. Il alerte sur leur violations et le climat politique avant la présidentielle de mai 2027. Le gouvernement et ses proches contestent son analyse et sa crédibilité. Les activistes, eux, estiment que présenter Zongo comme une menace diplomatique est en réalité une stratégie qui consiste à éviter le vrai débat.
Par Jules Bercy Igiraneza

data.title: Akbar Muderi : L’enfant de Ngozi qui a fait de Kigali son royaume
data.description: Imaginez Ngozi. L'air vif des hauts plateaux du nord. La terre rouge, les matins brumeux où les collines semblent retenir leur souffle. C'est là, le 28 avril 2003, que germe l'histoire. Pas dans l'or d'une académie clinquante, mais dans la poussière noble des terrains du Messager FC. C'est là qu'il apprend l'essentiel : le tacle qui ne pardonne pas, la relance juste, le sacrifice silencieux de celui qui joue pour que les autres brillent.

data.title: Yussuf Ndayishimiye : l’homme qui portait le brassard comme on porte une patrie
data.description:
Mardi le 29 septembre 2026. Le Stade Intwari n'était pas une forteresse. C'était une étuve à ciel ouvert, une arène sous les étoiles de Bujumbura. Et au milieu de ce brasier, il y avait lui : Yussuf Ndayishimiye de l'OGC Nice. 
 Ils l'avaient annoncé émoussé, usé par l'Europe. Ils s'étaient trompés de récit. Ce n'était pas un footballeur qui jouait un match. C'était un homme qui défendait une terre.

data.title: Région Centre/Gitega : Une médecine naturelle qui interroge
data.description: Méfiants envers un système de santé public à bout de souffle, des milliers d’habitants de Gitega se tournent désormais vers des centres privés et des associations qui proposent des traitements naturels mais qui sont très chers. Selon beaucoup de témoignages, ces officines dépouillent financièrement les familles et mettent leur santé en péril sous le regard impuissant des médecins.

data.title: Notice of Special General Meeting, Tonga Rugby Union Inc.
data.description: Nuku'alofa, Tonga Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated NOTICE OF SPECIAL GENERAL MEETING Date: Friday 9 th October 2026 Time: 6:00pm Venue: Mele Siu’ilikutapu Hall, Halaano To: All Members and Eligible Representatives of the Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated Dear Members, Notice is hereby given that a Special General Meeting ( SGM ) of the Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated ( TRU ) will be held on the date, time and at the venue specified above. The Special General Meeting is convened for the purpose of considering and determining the specific matters set out in this Notice. In accordance with Clause 5.2.3 of the TRU Constitution, the business of the Special General Meeting is expressly limited to the matters stated in this Notice. PURPOSE OF THE SPECIAL GENERAL MEETING The SGM will consider the following matters: Financial Reporting and the 2024 Audited Financial Statements; Current progress and status of the 2025 financial audit; and Election of the two remaining Elected Board Members. IMPORTANT NOTICE TO MEMBERS Members are requested to ensure that their duly appointed representatives attend the Special General Meeting. The Constitution provides that a quorum at a General Meeting, including a Special Meeting, consists of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the eligible representatives being present. Proxies are not permitted. The election of Board Members will be conducted in accordance with the Constitution, including the requirement for a secret ballot and preferential voting. The nominated candidates' relevant biographical information, work history and curriculum vitae should be circulated to Members in accordance with the Constitution. All nominations must be received by 4:00pm Thursday 8 th October 2026 , delivered in writing to the TRU Offices at FWC Building, Fasi-moe-Afi or by email david [dot] edwards [at] edwardslaw [dot] to . Please address the nominations to the Acting Chief Executive Officer. By Order of the Board of Governors David Lavulo Edwards Acting Chief Executive Officer Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated Date: Friday 2 nd October 2026 NUKU'ALOFA , KINGDOM OF TONGA WWW . TONGARUGBY . COM -- TONGA RUGBY UNION FANONGONONGO ʻO E FAKATAHA LAHI MAKEHE ʻAho: Falaite 'aho 9 'o 'Okatopa 2026 Taimi: 6:00pm Feituʻu: Mele Siuʻilikutapu Hall, Halaano Ki he: Kau fakafofonga kotoa pe ʻo e Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated Malo e lelei, ’E fakahoko ha Fakataha Lahi Makehe ( SGM ) ʻa e ‘Akapulu ‘Iunioni ‘A Tonga ( TRU ) ʻi he ʻaho, taimi mo e feituʻ u ʻoku lave ki ai ʻi ʻolunga. Ko e taumuʻa ʻo e fakataha ni ke vakaiʻi mo fai ha ngaahi tuʻutuʻuni ki he ngaahi kaveinga pau ʻoku fakaha atu ʻi lalo. Fakatatau ki he Kupu 5.2.3 ʻo e Konisitutone ʻo e ‘Akapulu ‘Iunioni ‘a Tonga, ʻe aleaʻi pe ʻe he kau memipa ‘oku kau ki he fakataha ni, ʻa e ngaahi kaveinga ʻoku lave ki ai heni. KO E ME ʻA TE TAU TALANOA KI AI ʻI HE SGM ʻE vakaiʻi ʻe he SGM ʻa e ngaahi meʻa ko ʻeni: Lipooti Paʻanga mo e Ngaahi Fakamatala Paʻanga ʻAotitaʻi ʻo e 2024; Fakalakalaka mo e tuʻunga lolotonga ʻo e ʻaotita fakapaʻanga ʻo e 2025; mo e Fili ʻo e ongo memipa fakamuimuitaha ʻo e Poate kuo fili. FAKATOKANGA MAHU ʻINGA KI HE KAU MEMIPA FAKATAHA Kataki ʻo fakapapauʻi ʻoku kau mai hoʻomou kau fakafofonga kuo fokotuʻu ki he Fakataha Lahi Makehe pea koe kau memipa totonu ia. Fakatatau ki he Konisitutone, ʻoku fie maʻ u ʻe ha Fakataha Lahi, kau ai ha Fakataha Makehe, ke ʻʻoua na a toe siʻi hifo ʻi he vahe tolu ʻe ua (2/3) ʻo e kau fakafofonga ʻoku ʻi ai ke ʻi ai ha kolomu. ʻOku ʻikai lava ke fakakau ʻa e kau fakafofonga ‘oku ‘ikai ko ha kau fakafofonga totonu. ʻE fili ʻa e kau memipa ʻo e Poate ʻo fakatatau ki he ngaahi tuʻutuʻuni ʻo e Konisitutone, kau ai ʻa e paloti fakapulipuli mo e fili ʻoku fie maʻu. ʻOku totonu ke vahevahe mai mei he kau kanititeiti kuo fokotu’u ha ngaahi fakamatala totonu mo falala’anga fekau’aki mo kinautolu, hange ko honau piokalafi, hisitolia ngaue mo ha CV , mo e kau memipa ʻo hange ko ia ʻoku fakamatalaʻi ʻi he Konisitutone. Kuo pau ke fakahu kotoa mai 'a e ngaahi fokotu'u kotoa pe ‘ikai to e tomui ‘I he taimi 4 efiafi Tusite ‘aho 8 'o 'Okatopa 2026 . Kataki ‘o fakahu mai e ngaahi fokotu’u ki he 'Ofisi 'o e TRU 'i he ‘Ofisi ‘a e Siasi Uesiliana Tau’ataina ‘o Tonga, Fasi-moe-Afi pe 'i he 'imeili david [dot] edwards [at] edwardslaw [dot] to . Kataki 'o fakatu’asila mai 'a e ngaahi fokotu'u ki he 'Ofisa Pule Lahi Le’ole’o. ʻI he Tuʻutuʻuni ʻa e Poate ʻo e Kau Talekita, David Lavulo Edwards ʻOfisa Pule Lahi Le’ole’o, Fokotuʻutuʻu ʻa eʻAkapulu ʻIunioni ʻa Tonga ʻAho: Falaite 'aho 2 'o 'Okatopa 2026 NUKU'ALOFA , KINGDOM OF TONGA WWW . data.translatedTitle: Notice of Special General Meeting, Tonga Rugby Union Inc.
data.translatedDescription: Nuku'alofa, Tonga Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated NOTICE OF SPECIAL GENERAL MEETING Date: Friday 9 th October 2026 Time: 6:00pm Venue: Mele Siu’ilikutapu Hall, Halaano To: All Members and Eligible Representatives of the Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated Dear Members, Notice is hereby given that a Special General Meeting ( SGM ) of the Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated ( TRU ) will be held on the date, time and at the venue specified above. The Special General Meeting is convened for the purpose of considering and determining the specific matters set out in this Notice. In accordance with Clause 5.2.3 of the TRU Constitution, the business of the Special General Meeting is expressly limited to the matters stated in this Notice. PURPOSE OF THE SPECIAL GENERAL MEETING The SGM will consider the following matters: Financial Reporting and the 2024 Audited Financial Statements; Current progress and status of the 2025 financial audit; and Election of the two remaining Elected Board Members. IMPORTANT NOTICE TO MEMBERS Members are requested to ensure that their duly appointed representatives attend the Special General Meeting. The Constitution provides that a quorum at a General Meeting, including a Special Meeting, consists of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the eligible representatives being present. Proxies are not permitted. The election of Board Members will be conducted in accordance with the Constitution, including the requirement for a secret ballot and preferential voting. The nominated candidates' relevant biographical information, work history and curriculum vitae should be circulated to Members in accordance with the Constitution. All nominations must be received by 4:00pm Thursday 8 th October 2026 , delivered in writing to the TRU Offices at FWC Building, Fasi-moe-Afi or by email david [dot] edwards [at] edwardslaw [dot] to . Please address the nominations to the Acting Chief Executive Officer. By Order of the Board of Governors David Lavulo Edwards Acting Chief Executive Officer Tonga Rugby Union Incorporated Date: Friday 2 nd October 2026 NUKU'ALOFA , KINGDOM OF TONGA WWW . TONGARUGBY . data.title: A Mboki, difficile de communiquer via le réseau Orange
data.description: Fr : Sa : Les habitants de Mboki (Haut-Mbomou) se plaignent du dysfonctionnement enregistrés ces derniers temps sur le réseau de l’opérateur téléphonique Orange Centrafrique. Alors que les appels passent difficilement et les transactions via Orange Money sont quasiment impossibles, les usagers demandent une intervention urgente. Emmanuel Samboli-Fils a recueilli leurs plaintes. L’article A Mboki, difficile de communiquer via le réseau Orange est apparu en premier sur Radio Ndeke Luka .

data.title: Cameroun : près de cinq tonnes de produits dangereux saisies dans le Nord
data.description: © DR 2,2 tonnes de whisky en sachets et 2,4 tonnes de cyanure ont été saisies par la Douane camerounaise mercredi 30 septembre 2026 à Garoua et à Djalingo. Des éléments de de la zone III de l’opération Halcomi IV ont opéré deux saisies de produits dangereux dans la région du Nord, faisant un volume de près de cinq tonnes. La plus importante saisie a eu lieu sur les berges de la Bénoué à Garoua. Les éléments coordonnés par le commandant Gonmoga Kaoga ont intercepté un débarquement en provenance du Nigeria. À l'intérieur : 37 sacs et 12 fûts, soit 2 450 kg de cyanure. Un produit chimique toxique, très prisé par les orpailleurs clandestins. Une telle quantité déversée dans la nature aurait suffi à décimer la faune aquatique de la Bénoué et à contaminer l'eau potable de toute une ville. La deuxième prise est survenue au poste de contrôle de Djalingo. Il s’agit de 22 ballots, soit 2 200 kg de whisky en sachets. Un produit dont la commercialisation est interdite au Cameroun. Ces alcools à bas prix, sans traçabilité, inondent les marchés et exposent les consommateurs à des intoxications. Ce sont au total, 4 650 kg de produits retirés de la circulation. Avec une telle réalisation en une seule journée, la Douane envoie un signal fort à la fin de sa campagne de sensibilisation nationale sur les boissons et produits sensibles : la phase de répression a commencé. Cet article Cameroun : près de cinq tonnes de produits dangereux saisies dans le Nord est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
